step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 58-year-old male traveler returning from Pakistan with acute severe rice-water diarrhea, shock, and AKI

step5_concept_grounding: Cholera caused by toxigenic Vibrio cholerae O1 El Tor, serotype Inaba

evidence_items.source_quote: The stool examination showed a watery-rice consistency, and the rapid diagnostic test (RDT) (Crystal VC, immunochromatographic One Step Rapid Test for Vibrio cholerae; Dipstick, Arkray Health Care Private, Surat, India) was positive.

The stool culture result, which was released on April 28, showed growth of V. cholerae O1 E1 Tor, subtype Inaba, which was fully sensitive to ampicillin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole.
evidence_items.target_concept: V. cholerae O1 El Tor, subtype Inaba

rationale: A 58-year-old male returned from Pakistan presenting with classic acute rice-water diarrhea, hypovolemic shock, and acute renal failure. Stool RDT was positive and stool culture confirmed Vibrio cholerae O1 El Tor, subtype Inaba — providing E1 disease-defining confirmatory laboratory evidence. All criteria for Valid Positive Diagnosis are fully satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old female presenting with abdominal pain and loose stools following household exposure to her father with cholera

step5_concept_grounding: Secondary cholera transmission caused by Vibrio cholerae O1 El Tor, subtype Inaba

evidence_items.source_quote: The team was informed that the rapid diagnostic stool test for the patient's daughter, who was 31 years old, was positive.

Her culture report was released on May 1; this also showed growth of a similar isolate of her father, V. cholerae O1 E1 Tor, subtype Inaba, fully sensitive to ampicillin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole.
evidence_items.target_concept: V. cholerae O1 El Tor, subtype Inaba

rationale: A 31-year-old female acquired infection after nursing her father with confirmed cholera. She presented with abdominal pain and loose stools; stool RDT was positive and stool culture isolated Vibrio cholerae O1 El Tor, subtype Inaba, establishing E1 laboratory-confirmed cholera. VPD criteria are fully satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 20-year-old male traveler returning from Bangladesh presenting with severe cholera, dehydration, and acute kidney injury

step5_concept_grounding: Acute cholera with severe volume depletion and acute kidney injury confirmed by stool culture

evidence_items.source_quote: A 20-year-old Asian male presented to Ibrahim Bin Hamad Obaidallah Hospital, Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates, on 24th March 2022 with abdominal pain and multiple watery diarrhea episodes for the last 24 hours.
evidence_items.target_concept: Acute watery diarrhea and dehydration after Bangladesh travel

evidence_items.source_quote: In the meantime, stool culture was positive for Vibrio cholerae on 28th March 2022.

rationale: A 20-year-old male returning from Bangladesh presented with profuse watery diarrhea, severe dehydration, and oliguric acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis. Stool culture was positive for Vibrio cholerae (E1 confirmatory laboratory evidence). All criteria for Valid Positive Diagnosis are met -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old female presenting with acute severe watery diarrhea, vomiting, and acute kidney injury

step5_concept_grounding: Cholera caused by Vibrio cholerae serogroup O1, biovar El Tor, serotype Ogawa

evidence_items.source_quote: On microscopic examination by hanging drop actively motile (darting motility) bacteria were observed.
evidence_items.target_concept: Darting motility characteristic of Vibrio cholerae

evidence_items.source_quote: Considering these findings, the clinical isolate (VF4E2) was identified as gas-producing  V. cholerae  serogroup O1, biovar El Tor, serotype Ogawa strain.
evidence_items.test_name: Stool culture, species-specific PCR, and slide agglutination serotyping
evidence_items.target_concept: V. cholerae serogroup O1, biovar El Tor, serotype Ogawa

rationale: A 30-year-old female presented with severe watery diarrhea (10 episodes in 24 hours), vomiting, and acute renal failure. Stool examination demonstrated darting motility, growth on TCBS, positive species-specific PCR, and slide agglutination confirming Vibrio cholerae serogroup O1, biovar El Tor, serotype Ogawa (E1 disease-defining confirmatory evidence). VPD criteria are fully satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 52-year-old male with colon cancer and large bowel obstruction diagnosed with non-diarrheal cholera by GI PCR

step5_concept_grounding: Non-diarrheal cholera diagnosed in the setting of mechanical large bowel obstruction, confirmed by GI multiplex PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool cultures were negative; however, the BioFire gastrointestinal polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panel of the stool was positive for E. coli (EAEC and EPEC) and V. cholerae.
The patient was diagnosed with non-diarrheal cholera in the setting of significant bowel obstruction secondary to colon cancer.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical and infectious disease diagnostic assessment
evidence_items.target_concept: Non-diarrheal cholera masked by bowel obstruction

evidence_items.source_quote: Infectious disease was also consulted, and the patient was started on 400 mg intravenous (IV) ciprofloxacin every 12 hours for five days. A repeat PCR panel six days later was negative, and the patient was able to proceed with the planned exploratory laparotomy with right colon mobilization and ileostomy creation, allowing for the resolution of his nausea and constipation.
evidence_items.test_name: Targeted antibiotic therapy and repeat GI PCR clearance
evidence_items.target_concept: Microbiological clearance of V. cholerae following ciprofloxacin

rationale: A 52-year-old male with metastatic colon adenocarcinoma and large bowel obstruction had stool BioFire GI multiplex PCR positive for Vibrio cholerae. Treating clinicians and infectious disease consultants explicitly diagnosed non-diarrheal cholera masked by anatomical obstruction and treated with ciprofloxacin, with follow-up PCR documentation of microbiological clearance. With validated molecular detection (PCR, E1) and explicit clinician diagnosis, VPD criteria are satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 47-year-old male returned traveler with severe cholera (>40 diarrheal episodes) complicated by stroke and STEMI

step5_concept_grounding: Severe cholera confirmed by stool culture precipitating hypovolemic stroke and myocardial infarction

evidence_items.source_quote: A 47-year-old Indian male presented to our government hospital in Doha, Qatar, in May 2024, complaining of persistent watery diarrhea, without hematochezia or mucoid content, lasting one day and exceeding over forty episodes.
evidence_items.target_concept: Profuse watery diarrhea exceeding 40 episodes in 24 hours

evidence_items.source_quote: On the third day of admission, stool culture confirmed the presence of Vibrio cholerae.
He has completed the antibiotic course for the treatment of cholera and is undergoing physical rehabilitation with physical and occupational therapy.
evidence_items.test_name: Antibiotic therapy completion and clinical outcome
evidence_items.target_concept: Completion of antibiotic therapy for cholera with diarrheal resolution

rationale: A 47-year-old male returned from India presenting with catastrophic profuse watery diarrhea (>40 episodes in 24 hours), severe dehydration, and hypotension, which triggered an acute ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction. Stool culture confirmed Vibrio cholerae (E1 confirmatory evidence), and the patient completed targeted antibiotic therapy for cholera with full gastrointestinal recovery. VPD is fully satisfied -> POSITIVE.

A 63-year-old male was admitted from 10 to 15 July 2016 with a 3-day history of voluminous diarrhea and stomach cramps; emergency department stool culture tested positive for Vibrio cholerae (E1_CONFIRMATORY). He was treated with antibiotics and intravenous fluids and achieved microbiological clearance prior to his subsequent readmission on 1 August 2016 for nosocomially transmitted Plasmodium falciparum malaria acquired during his cholera hospitalization. Assertion AFFIRMED, temporality RECENT_EPISODIC, clinical role SECONDARY_DIAGNOSIS / ACTIVE_COMORBIDITY, VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor_details.coreference_notes: 63-year-old male admitted for stool-culture-confirmed Vibrio cholerae enteritis from 10-15 July 2016 and readmitted on 1 August 2016 with hospital-acquired Plasmodium falciparum malaria.

step4_condition_matched: Confirmed Vibrio cholerae infection (cholera) with voluminous diarrhea and positive stool culture during hospitalization from 10-15 July 2016

evidence_items.source_quote: Prior to his admission for malaria, the patient was admitted for cholera between the 10-15 July. He had presented prior to the 10th with a 3-day history of voluminous diarrhoea and stomach cramps.
Upon testing in the emergency department, he tested positive on a stool culture for Vibrio cholerae.

step10_contradiction_notes: Three consecutive negative stool samples post-treatment document microbiological clearance following antibiotic therapy, not a contradiction of the confirmed cholera diagnosis.
